newsitem.title: USA: NYC sells $100 mln of bonds to retail in presale.
newsitem.headline: NYC sells $100 mln of bonds to retail in presale.

text.p: New York City, which plans to sell almost $1 billion of debt next week, said on Friday that retail investors had placed orders for up to approximately $100 million of bonds during the first day of the presale period.
"We typically get over $200 million of retail orders so $100 million is right on target," said a city official, who declined to be named.
Two maturities were oversubscribed, the 2000 and 2001 maturities, with the first one fetching a 4.75 percent yield, which matches its coupon, and the 2001 at five percent.
The retail scale, which typically is priced more aggressively than what later is offered to institutions, ranges from the 4.75 percent yield on the 2000 bonds to 6.18 percent for 2026.
The retail order period ends on Tuesday, one day before the issue comes to market.

Further, New York City said that about $94 million of the new money bonds with maturities from 2004 to 2009 will be insured by the Financial Guaranty Insurance Corp. "We get some net savings," the city official said.
